name: Desire (kāma)
description: Born of attachment to objects dwelt on, it gives rise to anger (2.62); the enemy, with anger, arising from rajas, all-devouring, greatly sinful, insatiable as fire; it covers knowledge, is seated in the senses, mind and understanding, and deludes the embodied one (3.37–40); it is what drives a person to sin against his will (3.36–37).
antidotes: Control the senses first; knowing what is beyond the understanding and steadying the self by the self, slay it (3.41–43)
Give up all desires and be content in the self (2.55, 2.71)

name: Anger (krodha)
description: Arises from desire and gives rise to delusion (2.62–63); named with desire as the enemy born of rajas (3.37); gone from the sage of steady mind (2.56).

name: Passion, attachment (rāga)
description: Set, with aversion, in each sense towards its object; a waylayer (3.34); gone from the sage of steady mind (2.56).
antidotes: Move among objects with senses free of passion and aversion, under control (2.64)

name: Aversion (dveṣa)
description: Paired with passion in each sense towards its object, a waylayer (3.34); the one of steady wisdom neither rejoices nor hates (2.57).
antidotes: Senses free of passion and aversion (2.64)

name: Attachment (saṅga)
description: Arises from dwelling on objects and leads to desire (2.62); attachment to action or to inaction is to be abandoned (2.47–48); those deluded by the guṇas are attached to the workings of the guṇas (3.29).
antidotes: Act unattached, for sacrifice and lokasaṃgraha (3.9, 3.19, 3.25); know that 'the guṇas move among the guṇas' (3.28)

name: Making the fruit of action one's motive (phalahetutva)
description: Being one whose motive is the fruit of action (karmaphalahetu) is forbidden (2.47); those whose motive is the fruit are pitiable (2.49).

name: Delusion (moha, saṃmoha)
description: The thicket of delusion the understanding must cross (2.52); arising from anger, it confuses memory (2.63); Arjuna's mind is bewildered about dharma (2.7); ahaṃkāra-delusion makes one think 'I am the doer' (3.27); desire deludes the embodied one (3.40).
antidotes: Knowledge of the imperishable embodied one (2.13, 2.30)
The brāhmī sthiti, after which one is not deluded (2.72)

name: The sense of 'I' as doer (ahaṅkāra)
description: Deluded by ahaṃkāra, one thinks 'I am the doer' though actions are done by the guṇas of prakṛti (3.27).
antidotes: Knowing the truth about guṇas and actions (3.28)

name: The sense of 'mine' (mamatva)
description: Its absence (nirmama) marks the one who attains peace (2.71); Arjuna is to fight free of it (3.30).
notes: The text names only its absence (nirmama); the abstract noun is supplied for the obstacle.

name: Grief (śoka)
description: Arjuna's grief, which makes him cast aside his bow (1.47) and which no kingdom could dispel (2.8).
antidotes: Knowledge that the embodied one is eternal and unslayable (2.11–30)
The certainty of death for the born (2.27)

name: Despondency (viṣāda)
description: Arjuna's despondency, from compassion, on seeing his kin, with its bodily signs (1.28–30; 2.1, 2.10).

name: Faintness of heart (kaśmala, klaibya, hṛdaya-daurbalya)
description: The faintness unworthy of the noble, not leading to heaven, bringing disgrace; unmanliness and petty weakness of heart (2.2–3).
antidotes: Cast it off and stand up (2.3)

name: Pitiable weakness (kārpaṇya)
description: The fault that strikes Arjuna's nature and leaves his mind bewildered about dharma (2.7).
antidotes: Asking a teacher as a disciple (2.7)

name: Greed (lobha)
description: The Kauravas' minds are overcome by greed so that they do not see the fault of destroying a family (1.38); Arjuna fears acting from greed for the pleasures of kingship (1.45).

name: Fear (bhaya)
description: Gone, with passion and anger, from the sage of steady mind (2.56); even a little of the yoga of understanding protects from great fear (2.40).

name: The turbulent senses
description: The turbulent senses forcibly carry away the mind even of a wise man who strives (2.60); the mind that follows the roving senses carries away wisdom like wind a ship on water (2.67).

name: Hypocrisy (mithyācāra)
description: Restraining the organs of action while sitting and recalling sense objects in the mind (3.6).
antidotes: Control the senses by the mind and act unattached (3.7)

name: Carping (asūyā)
description: Those who carp at Kṛṣṇa's teaching and do not follow it are deluded about all knowledge and lost (3.32).
